subject.title: fix(memory-wiki): reject oversized apply body files

question: Should `openclaw wiki apply synthesis --body-file` adopt a new hard 1 MiB public input limit, or should bounded reading follow an already established synthesis-body contract without rejecting formerly accepted files?
rationale: The fixed numeric limit is a user-visible compatibility policy, not a mechanical safety correction, and the available PR context does not establish that 1 MiB is the intended supported contract.

options.title: Define the supported body-size contract
options.body: Keep bounded regular-file handling, but set its limit from a maintainer-approved and documented synthesis-body contract with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

options.title: Approve the 1 MiB policy
options.body: Accept the breaking limit as intentional and require explicit upgrade wording and real behavior proof before merge.

options.title: Pause the cap proposal
options.body: Land no fixed rejection limit until an owner confirms the product need and supported size boundary.

recommendation.title: Define the supported body-size contract
recommendation.body: Keep bounded regular-file handling, but set its limit from a maintainer-approved and documented synthesis-body contract with fresh-install and upgrade proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Explicitly mentioned in the review timeline and the strongest available routing signal for the public CLI policy choice.
